why: The probe shows all three without-sentences, and further tries agreed: a material-less mesh added late is not drawn, a camera-less scene keeps 0 uniform writes over many frames, and an early default camera stays at radius 1 after frames.
The probe covers every step and every without-sentence, and a late receiveShadows stayed ignored after more frames, a ground move and a new material.
The probe shows setParent's effects and the duplicate draw; I also saw that removeFromScene(group) leaves a box linked by box.parent in the scene, and that the duplicate happens in either add order.

setMeshVisible works as probed, but 'it has to be created again' is false when the mesh is re-added before the next frame or the scene was never registered: then addToScene does not throw, the buffers are not destroyed and the mesh draws again.

Plain writes are uploaded not only when that light moves but whenever any light in the scene changes (setLightIntensity on another light uploaded lamp.intensity = 3), because the whole lights buffer is refilled.

'keeps m itself' lasts only until the next addThinInstance, which copies the matrices into a new array (so later edits of m plus flushThinInstances upload nothing), and that add also uploads an unflushed edit, so 'never uploaded' is false.
An in-place edit of scene.fog is uploaded at the next camera move (the scene uniforms are rewritten whenever the camera changes), so 'is not uploaded' holds only while the camera is still.

A late exclusion also takes effect without moving the mesh when a light is added to the scene (the box went to 2 lights of 3, and a control without an exclusion went to 3), so 'the mesh not moved, the exclusion is not applied' is too broad.
The probe shows the rebuild after a new material and the one plain copy without it, and flushThinInstances, a visibility toggle and five more frames did not rebuild it either.

The probe shows the toggle, the unlink and a late generator that is never sampled, which held after frames, moves and a new ground material; re-enabling after a caster moved while disabled redrew the map.
The probe shows both ways to add a caster and the addToScene-only case, and pushing a mesh that was already in the scene into the array also redrew the shadow map.

The probe shows 18 lights with setMaxLights(20) and only the first 16 uploaded and lighting the box without it; setMaxLights after building filled the buffer but left the shader array at 16, so the 'before' comment is right.
